areas.title: West woodland edge
areas.body: The nearer woodland supplies ordinary construction, repairs and fuel. Six abstract units recover each season; extraction is limited by standing material. No individual tree represents a stock unit. The outline marks a working clearing beside the wider stand, not a tree-by-tree harvesting boundary.

areas.title: Upper woodland
areas.body: More usable wood, but the longer unmaintained approach costs two units per worker. A staffed northern post supports the approach and removes that loss. Heavy use still depletes this stand. The outline marks the work clearing; trees and usable material belong to the surrounding stand.

households.body: We have experience choosing usable branches. Working beside people who shape them could reduce rejected pieces.
We practice shaping wood and checking bindings. Suitable pieces and repeated shared work matter more than owning a room.

posts.title: Landing watch
posts.body: The shelter observes the landing approach. Watch condition, ordinary watch staffing and maintained kits determine preparedness.

posts.title: Northern approach watch
posts.body: A supported observation point links the village to upper woodland. Two home watch workers support its longer approach; those adults cannot gather or build.

projects.title: Prepare shared wood work
projects.body: Adapt the use of the existing working room with a sorting rack and two working places. Shared sessions occupy two construction places and need two adults plus one timber for support each season. The room alone teaches nobody.

projects.title: Equip the local watch
projects.body: Commission four wooden watch kits: shaped staffs, carrying bindings and repair pieces. Pay two prepared sets as well as timber; finite project labor assembles and checks them. This is hypothetical preparedness, not evidence of an excavated weapon type.

projects.title: Support the northern observation point
projects.body: Prepare a modest observation and approach station. It needs two ordinary home watch workers and maintained watch facilities to improve upper-woodland access.

discoveries.title: Choosing workable wood
discoveries.body: The west yard household has practical woodland experience. Their knowledge is useful when paired with shaping practice; inspection itself produces nothing.

discoveries.title: Shaping and checking
discoveries.body: The upper household has shaping experience. A shared session in the working room can bring these complementary practices together.

discoveries.title: A shared preparation proposal
discoveries.body: After working together, the two households propose sustained sorting and shaping. Authorize cooperative sessions; after two supported seasons, the same two timber can yield two prepared sets instead of one. Two adults and one support timber remain necessary.

discoveries.title: The longer approach
discoveries.body: The upper stand loses two units per worker to its unsupported approach. A northern post and two home watch workers can remove that limit, but extra extraction depletes the stand. Compare retained woodland with the nearer sustainable harvest.

discoveries.title: Bindings and shafts need care
discoveries.body: Deployed kits lose one serviceable set every fourth season. A repair worker consumes one prepared set and one opening timber to restore one kit; training and repairs compete with other work.

ui.intro: Govern from above, investigate any subject here or in the world, then invest through ordinary commands. Every result resolves seasonally. Looking and waiting give no supplies.
ui.migration: Explicit adoption adds finite woodland, two-timber seasonal fuel demand, preparation, household experience and kit wear. Existing stocks, layouts, paid queues, principles and memories survive. Older modes remain unchanged until adoption. Save a backup for comparison.
ui.timing: Standing orders can change before resolution. Commissioned timber and prepared sets are already paid; cancellation refunds only the unused share. Forecast uses opening stock for fuel, preparation and repairs; new gathering cannot fund those bills this season.

ui.train: Commit an additional watch adult to training
ui.recover: Recovery: suspend preparation/training, pause unfinished commissions and restore reserve priority. Keep ordinary food, care and watch. Fuel is capped by opening timber; missed fuel costs wellbeing, never creates debt. Cancel unfinished kit work to recover its unused material share.
ui.growth: The existing town milestone and land growth-readiness review still apply. Explore Land for compact/outward choices.
ui.done: Observation chapter complete. Continue governing, inspect the planning record, or review land growth.
ui.kits_cost: Plus 2 prepared sets paid now; project work assembles 4 kits.
ui.training: Commit an additional watch adult to training
ui.store_note: Prepared sets bundle selected wood and gathered plant bindings. One full preparation duty includes collecting and working the bindings; no unlimited purchased parts exist. Store miniatures are stock markers, not individual inventories. Kits here record the whole inventory; the post shows its allocation.

tutorial.title: 1 · Follow the wood
tutorial.body: Inspect either woodland area. Read its assigned adults, stock and next-season extraction; the overview and the world tell the same story.

tutorial.title: 2 · Compare competing uses
tutorial.body: Inspect the material store. Construction is paid now; fuel, repairs and preparation use opening stock at resolution. Revise standing work before committing.

tutorial.title: 3 · Meet practical knowledge
tutorial.body: Ask about woodland and shaping work at the west yard and upper households, or their work areas. Find a complementary interest.

tutorial.title: 4 · Make room for cooperation
tutorial.body: Commission the shared room and schedule a shared session. After a real staffed season, ask at the working room and support the proposal. It costs places, material and finite adults.

tutorial.title: 5 · Prepare the watch
tutorial.body: Prepare material sets, commission the watch shelter and its kit initiative. Compare landing coverage with the northern approach; train only when reserves permit.

tutorial.title: 6 · Compare expectation and result
tutorial.body: Resolve a season with equipment. Read actual extraction, fuel and wear beside the next forecast. Watching the activities grants no additional output.

tutorial.title: 7 · Keep a way back
tutorial.body: Turn preparation off and review freed workers before resuming it. Pausing queues and training can also restore food reserves without erasing completed fabric.
